1	# Design
2	
3	Why the code is shaped this way, and what it rests on that is not guaranteed. Contracts are in
4	[api.md](api.md); numbers are in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md).
5	
6	## The transfer
7	
8	Peer windows are written with plain `cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync` into addresses obtained from torch
9	symmetric memory. That uses the copy engines and **no SMs**, which is the point: an SM-resident
10	collective cannot get a block slot while GEMMs hold every SM, and this one does not need one.
11	
12	Under a concurrent GEMM chain of the same duration, a **peer** copy overlaps it completely while a
13	**same-device** copy runs at close to full competition with it. So the zero-SM property is a
14	property of the *remote* copies. Two same-device copies remain: this rank's own share of the
15	transfer, and the copy-out on the copying path. That is the strongest argument for `out=` from
16	`empty_output()`, which removes the second one.
17	
18	`benchmark/bench_a2a.py --mode zerosm` is that A/B on a machine here:
19	
20	```bash
21	./tools/exclusive.sh 0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 -- torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 \
22	    benchmark/bench_a2a.py --mode zerosm
23	```
24	
25	The same bytes and the same `dst.copy_(src)`, once into a peer's window and once into this rank's
26	own memory. Each arm gets its own GEMM chain matched to that copy's length, because the same bytes
27	take several times longer to reach a peer than to reach local memory, so one chain cannot match
28	both. It goes through torch symmetric memory rather than through the operator, whose path also
29	contains two barrier kernels and a copy-out and so cannot attribute anything to the transfer. The
30	chain's own slowdown and the pair's wall clock are read together — a copy the chain starved reads
31	1.00× on the first column too — and the run's header says so. Two GPUs are the minimum.
32	
33	The sequence/head relayout is expressed as source and destination strides on those copies, so it
34	costs nothing beyond the transfer that had to happen anyway. That is why the baseline's two permute
35	kernels do not appear on this side at all.
36	
37	All the addressing lives in `src/a2a_plan.cc`, which has no CUDA, no torch and no communication
38	library in it. The layout contract can therefore be tested on a machine with no GPU
39	(`test/test_plan.py`), which is also the only correctness check CI can run.
40	
41	Uneven shards are the general case; even splits are `seq_splits = [s/P] * P`. There is one code
42	path, so there is one thing to get right.
43	
44	Remote copies are serialised on one stream because they all leave through the same egress and
45	separate streams only make them contend. This rank's own share crosses no link, so it runs on the
46	caller's stream alongside them.
47	
48	## Where the memory comes from
49	
50	Windows are torch symmetric-memory tensors, allocated with
51	`c10d::symmetric_memory::empty_strided_p2p` and registered with `rendezvous()`, which returns each
52	peer's address for that allocation. Both are `TORCH_API` and unchanged in signature from torch 2.10
53	through 2.13, so all of this lives in C++ (`src/group.cc`).
54	
55	Going through the allocator entry point directly, rather than through a `MemPool`, is what makes
56	the ordering argument simple. `rendezvous` is collective: every rank must reach it for the same
57	allocation at the same point in its own program. Nothing unrelated can be served from that entry
58	point, so the sequence of allocations this group makes is the sequence every rank makes, and the
59	SPMD call contract is the only thing it rests on.
60	
61	Memory is not committed up front and does not grow monotonically: dropping a window returns it to
62	the symmetric allocator. A window is matched by capacity and grows if a later call needs more, so a
63	call site costs one window at its high-water mark. Buffers from `empty_output()` are released when
64	the caller drops them -- the group holds a record of each, and prunes the records whose buffer no
65	longer has another holder.
66	
67	Two internal windows exist per dtype, one per stream the collectives run on. A window is
68	single-buffered, so two calls may share one only when the stream orders them — and the sync call
69	runs on the caller's stream while the async one runs on the comm stream.
70	
71	That ordering argument constrains every later path that allocates on demand: **what triggers the
72	allocation has to be a quantity every rank shares.** A shape, a dtype, a count of calls — all of
73	those are the same everywhere, because the SPMD contract says the sequence of calls is. A reference
74	count is not, and neither is anything derived from one. `lend=True` is where this bites: the group
75	lends one of four windows per dtype, and it picks by counting calls rather than by looking for a
76	window nobody holds, precisely because the second reads local state. Reference counts still appear
77	there, as the check that the rotation landed on a free window, never as the choice of which one.
78	
79	## The barrier
80	
81	A one-block spin kernel, publishing with a release store and waiting with an acquire load, over a
82	device-resident epoch counter. Both live in the allocation's own signal pad, so the handshake state
83	is per window by construction.
84	
85	The epoch is on the device rather than computed on the host so that a CUDA-graph capture replays
86	correctly — a host-computed epoch would bake a constant into the graph and every replay would be
87	satisfied by stale state. `test/distributed/cudagraph.py` holds this: over eight replays with one
88	rank deliberately skewed, the epoch advances by two per replay (one per barrier) and every replay
89	is bit-exact.
90	
91	What is capturable is narrower than that argument alone suggests, and the boundary is a property of
92	the allocation rather than of the handshake:
93	
94	- the **sync** call, on a shape whose window **already exists**. Allocating one is
95	  `empty_strided_p2p` + `rendezvous` + `zero_()`, none of which is legal inside a capture, so a
96	  first call for a new shape ends the capture rather than being recorded.
97	- the **async** call is out entirely: `stage()` waits on an event recorded by the previous,
98	  uncaptured call, and a cross-graph event dependency invalidates the capture.
99	
100	Warm every shape eagerly before capturing, and pass `out=` from `empty_output()` so the graph writes
101	a fixed address rather than one from its private pool.
102	
103	`cuStreamWriteValue64` / `cuStreamWaitValue64` would remove the kernel launches from the path and
104	were tried. They measured worse under concurrent compute — overlap fell from +34% to −28% — which
105	is the regression this operator exists to avoid, and that remains the reason not to use them. The
106	CUDA memop documentation offers a mechanism: ordering established through those APIs "is not
107	visible to CUDA", so a blocked memop is invisible to the work scheduler and concurrent kernels can
108	be queued behind it.
109	
110	An earlier version of this note also blamed `CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_CAN_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES`. That
111	attribute gates only the `_FLUSH` variants, which exist for writes arriving over PCIe from a NIC.
112	NVSHMEM's on-stream wait does require it and does use `FLUSH`; NCCL's CE wait uses neither. The
113	attribute is therefore not by itself a reason the waiting form cannot be used over NVLink.
114	
115	The spin kernel's inline PTX needs only `sm_70`.
116	
117	## Tracing
118	
119	The group is a torchbind object and no fake class is registered for it, so Dynamo cannot represent
120	it in a graph and breaks on the call. Registering one would mean giving the group a meaningful
121	fake — the windows, their peer addresses and the rendezvous behind them — which is state a trace
122	cannot stand in for.
123	
124	What does work is shape propagation: the functional op has an explicit Meta kernel, so `FakeTensor`
125	and AOTAutograd see the output shape without touching a device, and the backward traces like any
126	other op. `empty_output()` refuses to be traced at all rather than being recorded: it is a
127	collective allocation, and replaying a trace would put the rendezvous where the graph places it
128	rather than where every rank's own program reaches it. Call it eagerly and pass the buffer in.
129	
130	## What this rests on that is not documented
131	
132	**A completed copy-engine write is visible at the destination by the time a later kernel's release
133	store announcing it arrives.** No vendor document says so:
134	
135	- the CUDA API reference defines memcpy completion as a *host-side* property;
136	- the Programming Guide's cross-device ordering guarantee is scoped to the NULL stream and is
137	  withdrawn for async copies on a non-default stream;
138	- PTX scopes `.release` to "prior operations from the current thread", which a copy-engine transfer
139	  is not;
140	- no vendor documents the ordering either way.
141	
142	We are not alone in relying on it, which is worth knowing before deciding how much to worry.
143	NVIDIA ships this exact shape in at least two places, both with *weaker* ordering than ours:
144	NVSHMEM's on-stream `signal_op` takes a CE payload and then publishes the flag from a
145	`<<<1,1>>>` kernel doing a bare `atomicAdd_system` with no fence (`sync.cpp` → the
146	`signal_op_kernel` it falls back to whenever the op is `SIGNAL_ADD`), and TransformerEngine's
147	userbuffers does the same in `ring_exchange`, which is its shipping default. Ours at least
148	publishes with `red.release.sys`.
149	
150	NCCL is the one that avoids the shape rather than accepting it. Its kernel-less CE collectives
151	(`ce_coll.cc`, `NCCL_CTA_POLICY_ZERO`, NCCL 2.28+) publish the flag as an 8-byte device-to-device
152	`cudaMemcpyAsync` on the same stream as the payload and wait with `cuStreamWaitValue32`, so the
153	flag rides the engine the data rode. That is the shape to move to if this assumption ever has to
154	go; the cost, and why it is not obviously better, is in the barrier section below.
155	
156	It holds in testing, which is evidence and not a guarantee.
157	`test/distributed/ce_ordering.py` tests it and arms its own negative control on every run, so the
158	test cannot silently stop testing.
159	
160	## Why NVLink only
161	
162	Over PCIe the operator is correct and slower than `torch.distributed`, by an amount that is not
163	stable: across a socket boundary it ran at 0.62× the baseline on one PCIe node and 0.14× on
164	another. Nothing is averaged, because the two nodes disagree by 5×. Numbers in
165	[benchmark.md](benchmark.md), "Why not PCIe".
166	
167	The fabric is not what differs: flat peer copies reach the same bandwidth on both nodes. What
168	differs is what the pitched (strided) copy pattern extracts from it, which degrades over PCIe by an
169	amount that depends on the switch layout below the socket. So there the transfer stage itself is
170	the slow part — the opposite of the NVLink case, and the reason the relayout-in-strides trade stops
171	paying.
172	
173	Matching NCCL there means a shared-host-memory transport with a second handshake — a new transport,
174	not a scheduling change, worth nothing on NVLink. Not built, so the constructor refuses the
175	topology instead of pretending.
176	
177	## The async result
178	
179	`all_to_all_4d_async` returns an `AsyncCollectiveTensor` registered against torch's work registry,
180	so the first aten op on the result waits by itself. The registry keys on the output's **storage**,
181	so a registry entry belongs to that call.
182	
183	When the registry is unavailable in the linked libtorch, the same function returns a handle with an
184	explicit `.wait()`. A result that is simply dropped leaves an entry behind; torch prints a count of
185	the survivors at process exit.
186	
187	The sync collective stays on the caller's stream rather than the comm stream. Routing it through
188	would cost two event hops per call, which is comparable to the collective itself.
189	
190	## Removed, and why
191	
192	Earlier versions carried more surface than they could defend:
193	
194	- **NVSHMEM.** It supplied the same thing torch symmetric memory does — VMM allocations with peer
195	  addresses — at the cost of a bootstrap, a strided-team split, an entire pool allocator, two
196	  undocumented `hostlib_` entry points chosen to avoid a symbol clash with torch's own bundled
197	  NVSHMEM, and a rule that live groups must partition the job (unenforceable, because the check
198	  would have to run on ranks that never reach the constructor). None of that survives the swap.
199	- **A borrowed entry point** whose result was the window itself, under a lifetime contract nothing
200	  enforced. `out=` from `empty_output()` gives the same saving with the buffer's lifetime in the
201	  caller's hands.
202	- **`tag`.** It existed to keep concurrently-live results in separate windows. The copying path
203	  gives each call its own tensor and the zero-copy path uses the caller's own buffer, so there is
204	  nothing left to disambiguate.
205	- **`reserve()` / `seal()`.** They existed because the old pool's allocation was collective and
206	  stream-synchronising, which deadlocked if it happened mid-call. Allocation is still collective,
207	  but the deadlock it fed on — a spin barrier deliberately left in flight — went with the deferred
208	  closing handshake.
209	- **A `torch.distributed` fallback group** for the topology above. The answer there is to use
210	  `torch.distributed` directly.
211

84	Returning that quietly would be indistinguishable from a caller who wanted no gradient, so a
85	grad-requiring input under grad mode raises instead. Use `out=` in inference or under
86	`torch.no_grad()`, where it is accepted; use the plain call inside a training graph.
87	
88	**`seq_splits[p]` / `head_splits[p]`** are rank p's sequence and head shard. Pass **both or
89	neither**, identical on every rank, matching the shape handed in. Neither means even shards, and
90	the scattered axis must then divide (`n_global % ws` for mode 0, `s_global % ws` for mode 1). Both
91	lets shards differ arbitrarily, which is what lets a caller drop sequence padding.
92	
93	### Raises
94	
95	`RuntimeError`, from validation that runs **before the call's first barrier**, so a rejected
96	argument leaves no rank waiting on peers that did not reject it: the group already `destroy()`ed;
97	`x` not 4D or not CUDA, or on a device other than the group's; dtype not in the dtype list above;
98	`d * elem_size` not 16 B-aligned; `mode` not 0 or 1; one of the splits without the other, or splits
99	contradicting `x`'s shape; no splits and the scattered axis does not divide; every rank's shard
100	empty, so the call moves no data; `out` not contiguous CUDA, on another device, or its dtype or
101	shape not the output's; `x` overlapping the window, or `out` partially overlapping it.
102	
103	`world_size` outside `[1, 8]` is refused by the constructor, so no call reaches it.
104	
105	## `all_to_all_4d_async(x, *, mode=0, out=None, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None, lend=False)`
106	
107	The same call on the group's high-priority comm stream, returning immediately.
108	
109	**Not differentiable, and it refuses rather than pretending.** An `AsyncCollectiveTensor` is built
110	with `requires_grad` on the wrapper, which makes it a leaf: autograd runs above the subclass and
111	never sees the wrapped tensor's history, so a `backward()` through it would run to completion and
112	leave `x.grad` as `None`. A grad-requiring input raises instead. Use `all_to_all_4d`.
113	
114	The result is an `AsyncCollectiveTensor`: `.wait()` returns the plain tensor, and so does the **first use by any
115	aten op** — either way the caller's stream waits on the comm stream's completion event GPU-side,
116	and the host does not block. A **view op** does not wait; it re-wraps.
117	
118	**Wait on, or use, every result.** A dropped one leaves its entry in torch's work registry and its
119	CUDA event behind; torch prints a count of the survivors at exit. `out=` is the hole, since reading
120	your own `out` never touches the registry — read the returned wrapper.
121	
122	The input is staged into a persistent per-`(shape, dtype)` buffer on the caller's stream, so `x` is
123	never retained cross-stream. That costs one device copy per call. Buffers of one shape form a pool
124	of **4**, so that many same-shaped calls can be in flight before one waits for another to retire.
125	
126	### `lend=True`
127	
128	`out=`'s saving without a buffer of your own: the peers write a window the group holds, the result
129	**is** that window, and there is no copy-out. Mutually exclusive with `out=` — passing both raises.
130	Not differentiable, like the rest of this call.
131	
132	The group keeps **4 windows per dtype and takes them in order**, one per call. Which window a call
133	fills has to be the same on every rank, since the transfer addresses the peers through that window
134	and the barrier through its signal pad; a rotation driven by the call count is the same everywhere,
135	and anything read off local reference counts is not.
136	
137	So the bound is a rule, not a hint: **at most 4 lent results alive at once, and every rank must drop
138	them at the same point in its own program.** A fifth live one raises. A rank that dropped a result
139	its peers still hold does not raise — it fills a window they are not reading, which is the hang this
140	page opens with.
141	
142	Use it when a result is consumed and released within the step that issued it, which is what a
143	split q/k/v exchange does. Keep a result across steps and `empty_output()` with `out=` is the fit.
144	
145	On a libtorch with no `c10d::register_work` there is no registry to bind to, and this returns a
146	`CompletedHandle` instead: same `.wait()`, correct results, no overlap. A distinct type, so it is
147	visible.
148	
149	The sync and async calls do not share a window, so mixing them is safe.
150	
151	## `empty_output(x, *, mode=0, seq_splits=None, head_splits=None) -> Tensor`
152	
153	A buffer shaped like `all_to_all_4d(x, mode=...)`'s output, in symmetric memory. Passing it back as
154	`out=` removes the copy-out.
155	
156	**Collective**, so allocate outside the loop and reuse it. It is an ordinary tensor: keep it across
157	steps, free it when you like, and it may outlive the group.
158	
159	It is larger than it looks. Under uneven splits the window has to hold the **largest** rank's
160	output, because the peer offsets only line up while every rank allocates the same size; the tensor
161	you get is a view of that allocation's dense prefix.
162	
163	## `destroy() -> None`
164	
165	Releases the group's windows and its transfer stream. All ranks must call it together. Buffers
166	from `empty_output()` are unaffected — they are yours.
167	
168	## Environment
169	
170	Nothing is read from the environment on the collective path. On a machine whose Fabric Manager
171	cannot bind NVLink SHARP, NCCL needs `NCCL_NVLS_ENABLE=0`; that affects the `torch.distributed`
172	bootstrap, not this operator. See [install.md](install.md).
173

# Quick start

## Wrapping attention

The two calls bracket attention: mode 0 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, mode 1 trades
it back.

```python
import os

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

dist.init_process_group("nccl")
torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
ws = dist.get_world_size()

group = UlyssesGroup()          # collective; refuses a group that is not NVLink-joined

def attention_block(qkv):       # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
    qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)      # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
    out = attention(qkv)                        # each rank now holds whole sequences
    return group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)     # -> (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
```

Pack q, k and v into one collective when you can: the last dim is just `3 * head_dim`, and one
call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three.

## Removing the copy-out

The default returns a tensor the call allocated, which costs one flat device-to-device copy out of
the window. Give it a symmetric buffer instead and the peers write that buffer directly:

```python
buf = group.empty_output(qkv, mode=0)     # collective: allocate ONCE, outside the loop
for step in range(steps):
    y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, out=buf)   # no copy-out; y is buf
```

`buf` is an ordinary tensor you own. It is overwritten by the next call that uses it, so use one
buffer per concurrent call.

`out=` gives up the gradient: the result comes back with no `grad_fn` and no `requires_grad`, and
nothing raises. Use it in inference and under `torch.no_grad()`; inside a training graph, call
without `out=`.

## Overlapping with compute

The transfer uses no SMs, so it can run underneath compute. Submit it, do the compute, then use the
result — the first aten op on it inserts the wait GPU-side.

```python
y = group.all_to_all_4d_async(qkv, mode=0)   # inference only: raises if qkv requires grad
h = some_gemm_chain(other_input)             # runs while the copy engines move qkv
y = y.wait()                                 # or just use y; the first op waits by itself
```

The async form is not differentiable and refuses a grad-requiring input rather than dropping the
gradient, so in a training step this is the sync call's job.

Wait on, or use, every async result. A dropped one leaves an entry in torch's work registry.

## Dropping the sequence padding

Sharding a sequence usually means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size and padding the
tail, so every rank holds the same length. Those padded tokens then ride through attention and the
collective on every layer of every step. Pass the real per-rank lengths instead:

```python
s = 75827                                    # does not divide by ws
seq_splits = [s // ws + (1 if p < s % ws else 0) for p in range(ws)]
head_splits = [n_global // ws] * ws

y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, seq_splits=seq_splits, head_splits=head_splits)
```

Both lists or neither, identical on every rank. Uneven is the general path here, not a slow one.

## Under 2-D parallelism

`process_group` takes any subgroup — the sp slice of a tp × sp mesh, with no restriction on which
ranks it contains:

```python
sp_group = mesh["sp"].get_group()
group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)
```

## What will hang you

Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. The first call with a new shape allocates a
window, and that allocation is collective — if one rank takes a branch the others do not, it waits
there. This is the same discipline `torch.distributed` collectives already require.

## Coming from another Ulysses

`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention` and `LongContextAttention` are attention modules, and
sglang's `usp.py` is called from one; this is only the collective, so a port replaces the module
with the two calls above plus your own attention. `scatter_idx` / `gather_idx` map to `mode`, the
`torch.autograd.Function` wrapper is deleted rather than translated, and a caller on `(s, b, n, d)`
still owes a transpose. Call by call: [migration.md](migration.md).

## Checking the machine

```bash
fast-ulysses doctor
```

Prints the build, the devices, and the pairwise NVLink matrix. A group spanning a pair marked `N`
is refused at construction.

1	# Migration
2	
3	Coming from DeepSpeed-Ulysses, sglang's `usp.py` or yunchang: what each call becomes here, what your
4	layout costs, and what this library does not have.
5	
6	One structural difference first. All three of those ship an **attention module** —
7	`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention`, `LongContextAttention` — that owns the q/k/v exchange,
8	the attention call and the output exchange. fast-ulysses ships **only the collective**. You replace
9	one module with two calls and your own attention kernel. `examples/dit_attention.py` is that shape
10	end to end, forward and backward.
11	
12	Left-hand cells below were read from: DeepSpeed `deepspeed/sequence/layer.py` and
13	`deepspeed/runtime/sequence_parallel/ulysses_sp.py`; sglang
14	`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/usp.py` and
15	`runtime/distributed/{communication_op.py,device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py}`;
16	yunchang `yunchang/comm/all_to_all.py`, `yunchang/ulysses/attn_layer.py`, `yunchang/globals.py` and
17	`yunchang/hybrid/attn_layer.py`. Read on the default branch on 2026-08-10, not from a pinned
18	release; yunchang's default branch and its latest tag, 0.6.4, are identical in `comm/all_to_all.py`.
19	Check your installed version before trusting a row.
20	
21	## The shape of the replacement
22	
23	```python
24	# DeepSpeed
25	from deepspeed.sequence.layer import DistributedAttention
26	
27	self.dist_attn = DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)
28	out = self.dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx)   # 0 -> (b, s, n, d), 1 -> (s, b, n, d)
29	```
30	
31	```python
32	# here -- qkv packed into the last axis, so two collectives stay two collectives
33	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
34	
35	group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)   # collective; build once, not per call
36	
37	# qkv is this rank's shard, (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
38	qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)   # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
39	q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
40	out = local_attn(q, k, v)                # your kernel, on whole sequences
41	out = group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)   # (b, s_global, n_local, hd) -> (b, s_local, n, hd)
42	```
43	
44	## From DeepSpeed-Ulysses
45	
46	| what you write today | what it becomes here |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| `DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)` — the collective only; you call `local_attn` yourself |
49	| `dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx=0)` | `all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0)` per tensor, or one call on q/k/v packed into a `3 * head_dim` last axis |
50	| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, 2, g, batch_dim_idx)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
51	| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, g, 2, batch_dim_idx)` — the output call, indices swapped, `g` in `{0, 1}` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
52	| three `_SeqAllToAll.apply` calls, one each for q, k, v | one call on a `3 * head_dim` last axis: one handshake instead of three, same bytes |
53	| `batch_dim_idx=1`, i.e. `(s, b, n, d)` | not accepted — transpose first, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
54	| `uneven_heads_all2all`, sizes derived from `get_num_kv_heads()`, `assert async_op == False` | `head_splits=[...]` that you pass, on the sync **and** the async call |
55	| `UlyssesSPAttentionHF` (ALST), strictly `(sl, bs, hc, hs)` | not accepted — transpose in and back out, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
56	| the `_SeqAllToAll` `torch.autograd.Function` wrapper | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |
57	| `UlyssesSPDataLoaderAdapter`, `register_with_transformers()`, `UlyssesSPFwdLossBwdWithLogits` | no counterpart — this is a collective, not a training integration |
58	
59	`DistributedAttention.forward`'s fourth parameter is `batch_dim_idx`, positional and required. If
60	your call site passes an attention mask there — the DeepSpeed tutorial snippet and
61	Megatron-DeepSpeed's non-flash branch both do — the layout selection is reading a tensor, and you
62	should settle what that call actually did before porting it.
63	
64	## From sglang `usp.py`
65	
66	| what you write today | what it becomes here |
67	| --- | --- |
68	| `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
69	| `_usp_output_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
70	| `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=1)`, i.e. `(b, n, s, d)` | not accepted — transpose first, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
71	| `_usp_input_all_to_all_qkv` (4D q/k/v) / `_usp_input_all_to_all_packed_qkv` (3D q/k/v) — both pack the three into one collective | one `all_to_all_4d` on `(b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)`, which is the same packing expressed as a shape |
72	| `_usp_input_all_to_all_varlen(x, seq_lens, head_dim=2)` and its output form | `seq_splits=seq_lens, head_splits=[n_global // ws] * ws` on the ordinary call; there is no separate varlen entry point |
73	| `sequence_model_parallel_all_to_all_4D(x, scatter_dim=2, gather_dim=1)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
74	| `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D.apply(...)` | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |
75	| `_a2a_staging_buffer(role, shape, dtype, device)`, bypassed when `torch.is_grad_enabled()` | nothing to pass or plumb: windows are cached internally per dtype and stream, with grad on or off |
76	| `_ipc_all_to_all_4d`, gated to `world_size == 2` | the copy-engine path is the only path, at every `world_size` in `[1, 8]` |
77	
78	sglang has two implementations of this collective — `usp.py`'s plain functions, with no gradient
79	support, and `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D`, which is differentiable and reaches the same result
80	through different permutes. Both map to the same two calls here.
81	
82	## From yunchang / long-context-attention
83	
84	| what you write today | what it becomes here |
85	| --- | --- |
86	| `set_seq_parallel_pg(...)` writing the module-level `PROCESS_GROUP.ULYSSES_PG` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_pg)` per instance; no global state |
87	| `UlyssesAttention(sp_pg, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=1, attn_type=AttnType.FA)` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_pg)` plus your own attention call — there is no `attn_type` |
88	| `SeqAllToAll4D.apply(pg, x, 2, 1)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
89	| `SeqAllToAll4D.apply(pg, x, 1, 2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
90	| `all_to_all_4D(x, 2, 1, group=pg)` — the plain function, no grad | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)`, which does carry grad |
91	| `all_to_all_5D(x, scatter_idx=3, ...)` on `(bs, s, 3, hc, hs)` | no 5D entry point — fold the qkv axis, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
92	| `use_pack_qkv=True`, `torch.cat([q, k, v])` on the batch axis — the branch then calls `.continous()`, which is not a tensor method, so it raises `AttributeError` before the collective | that cat works unchanged (`b` becomes `3 * b`); packing into `3 * head_dim` is the same one handshake |
93	| `use_sync=True` | no counterpart; nothing here inserts a `torch.cuda.synchronize()` |
94	| `LongContextAttention(..., ring_impl_type=...)`, ulysses × ring | no counterpart. Ulysses only |
95	| a head count that does not divide `world_size` (fails at yunchang's `reshape`) | `head_splits=[...]` |
96	
97	yunchang enforces the index pair — only `(2, 1)` and `(1, 2)` are implemented, anything else raises —
98	so its two directions map one-to-one onto the two modes.
99	
100	## scatter_idx / gather_idx, and mode
101	
102	`mode=0` scatters heads and gathers sequence: `(b, s_local, n_global, d) -> (b, s_global, n_local, d)`.
103	`mode=1` is the inverse.
104	
105	| what selects the direction today | here |
106	| --- | --- |
107	| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx = 2` | `mode=0` |
108	| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx` in `{0, 1}` | `mode=1` |
109	| yunchang `scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=1` | `mode=0` |
110	| yunchang `scatter_idx=1, gather_idx=2` | `mode=1` |
111	| sglang `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=0` |
112	| sglang `_usp_output_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=1` |
113	| sglang `scatter_dim=2, gather_dim=1` | `mode=0` |
114	
115	Two traps in the left column:
116	
117	- **DeepSpeed's `gather_idx` does not select the layout on the even path.** It is never passed to
118	  `_generate_layout_params`, and in `single_all_to_all` it is forwarded only to
119	  `uneven_heads_all2all`; the direction is chosen by the predicate `scatter_idx < 2` alone.
120	  `gather_idx` matters only because the output call swaps it into `scatter_idx`. Map by
121	  `scatter_idx`, not by the argument names.
122	- **yunchang's `all_to_all_4D` docstring contradicts its own signature** (it says the defaults are
123	  `scatter_idx=1, gather_idx=2`; the signature is `2, 1`). Read the signature.
124

126	
127	This library takes **4D `(b, s, n, d)` and nothing else.** No 3D form, no 5D form, no
128	`batch_dim_idx`, no `head_dim` argument. That is a real constraint and it is where a migration
129	costs something.
130	
131	| the layout you have | what it costs here |
132	| --- | --- |
133	| `(b, s, n, d)` — sglang `head_dim=2`, yunchang, DeepSpeed `batch_dim_idx=0` | nothing; this is the input |
134	| `(3, s, n, d)` — a q/k/v stack whose dim 0 is not batch | nothing; `b = 3`, and q, k, v are exchanged independently |
135	| `(s, n * d)` contiguous 3D | `x.view(1, s, n, d)` — a view, no copy |
136	| `(b, n, s, d)` — sglang `head_dim=1`, and sglang's default | `x.transpose(1, 2)` in, and back out after the call. 140	`.contiguous()` is applied internally, so writing it yourself changes nothing — but a transposed
141	input is copied either way, by you or by the op.
142	
143	The 5D fold has a shortcut that looks right and is not. `(b, s, 3, n, d)` reshapes to
144	`(b, s, 3 * n, d)` for free, but an even split then cuts that merged axis into contiguous chunks, so
145	a rank receives a mixture of q, k and v heads rather than the same head slice of each.
146

148	
149	DeepSpeed's `_SeqAllToAll` and yunchang's `SeqAllToAll4D` are `torch.autograd.Function`s whose
150	`backward` re-applies the forward with `scatter_idx` and `gather_idx` swapped. `all_to_all_4d` is
151	differentiable in C++, so the wrapper is deleted, not translated: the backward is the other `mode`.
152	
153	The convention differs where it matters. Those libraries express the backward as *swap the two
154	indices*; here it is *the other mode with the **same** splits*. Identical while shards are even,
155	not once they are not — why, in [api.md](api.md).
156	
157	`examples/dit_attention.py` is the worked case — one DiT attention block, sequence-parallel, an
158	ordinary `nn.Module`, checked for both output and input gradient against the same block with no
159	sequence parallelism, then run through five optimiser steps:

163	```

171	
172	| library | uneven support |
173	| --- | --- |
174	| DeepSpeed | heads only, via `uneven_heads_all2all`, with sizes derived from `get_num_kv_heads()` rather than passed by the caller; `assert async_op == False`. No uneven sequence |

176	| yunchang | none. `hc // world_size` then a `reshape`, so a non-divisible head count fails at the reshape with no explicit check |
177	| here | `seq_splits` / `head_splits`, both or neither, identical on every rank, on the sync and async calls alike. Even splits are the special case of the same code path, not a fast path beside it |
178	
179	What that buys: sharding a sequence normally means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size,
180	and those padded tokens then ride through attention and both collectives on every layer of every
181	step. Dropping the pad costs the baseline **5–11%** and costs this path **1.00–1.03×** — every
182	shape, every machine. Table in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md), "Removing the sequence padding".
183	
184	## The measured baseline is the path you are leaving
185	
186	The `BASE` column in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md) is not a strawman built for the comparison. It is
187	sglang's `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` restated permute for permute —
188	`benchmark/bench_a2a.py:baseline_stages`:
189	
190	```python
191	y = x.permute(2, 0, 1, 3).contiguous().flatten()
192	dist.all_to_all_single(recv, y, group=pg)

194	```
195	
196	`test/distributed/correctness.py:reference_even` holds this operator **bit-exact** against that same
197	path, so the two are checked to be the same function before either is timed. The **1.60–2.17×** in
198	that document, and the per-machine multipliers in the README, are therefore measured against exactly
199	what a sglang or DeepSpeed caller runs today, and the `relayout%` column — **46.9–60.0%** of the
200	baseline — is the two permute kernels that do not exist on this side.
201	
202	Two qualifications, so the number is read for what it is:
203	
204	- The benchmark measures `mode=0`. Upstream sglang's `mode=1` equivalent, `_usp_output_all_to_all`

208	  so against *current* sglang the saving on the mode-1 half is smaller than the table implies, by an
209	  unknown amount. Mode 0's two permutes are real on both.
210	- The multiplier moves with world size, for the baseline's reason rather than this operator's — at
211	  ws=4 it is 2.6–2.8× on B200 and 1.7–1.9× on H100. Compare `relayout%` across group sizes, not
212	  the multiplier; the table and the reason are in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md).
213	
214	## What this does not have
215	
216	Check this list before you start, not after.
217

219	- **PCIe.** `UlyssesGroup()` refuses a group whose GPUs are not NVLink-joined; `require_nvlink=False`

239	- Build the group **once** and keep it. It holds the windows, the plan cache and the comm stream.

# Migration

Coming from DeepSpeed-Ulysses, sglang's `usp.py` or yunchang: what each call becomes here, what your
layout costs, and what this library does not have.

One structural difference first. All three of those ship an **attention module** —
`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention`, `LongContextAttention` — that owns the q/k/v exchange,
the attention call and the output exchange. fast-ulysses ships **only the collective**. You replace
one module with two calls and your own attention kernel. `examples/dit_attention.py` is that shape
end to end, forward and backward.

Left-hand cells below were read from: DeepSpeed `deepspeed/sequence/layer.py` and
`deepspeed/runtime/sequence_parallel/ulysses_sp.py`; sglang
`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/usp.py` and
`runtime/distributed/{communication_op.py,device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py}`;
yunchang `yunchang/comm/all_to_all.py`, `yunchang/ulysses/attn_layer.py`, `yunchang/globals.py` and
`yunchang/hybrid/attn_layer.py`. Read on the default branch on 2026-08-10, not from a pinned
release; yunchang's default branch and its latest tag, 0.6.4, are identical in `comm/all_to_all.py`.
Check your installed version before trusting a row.

## The shape of the replacement

```python
# DeepSpeed
from deepspeed.sequence.layer import DistributedAttention

self.dist_attn = DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)
out = self.dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx)   # 0 -> (b, s, n, d), 1 -> (s, b, n, d)
```

```python
# here -- qkv packed into the last axis, so two collectives stay two collectives
from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup

group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)   # collective; build once, not per call

# qkv is this rank's shard, (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)   # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
out = local_attn(q, k, v)                # your kernel, on whole sequences
out = group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)   # (b, s_global, n_local, hd) -> (b, s_local, n, hd)
```

## From DeepSpeed-Ulysses

| what you write today | what it becomes here |
| --- | --- |
| `DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)` — the collective only; you call `local_attn` yourself |
| `dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx=0)` | `all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0)` per tensor, or one call on q/k/v packed into a `3 * head_dim` last axis |
| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, 2, g, batch_dim_idx)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, g, 2, batch_dim_idx)` — the output call, indices swapped, `g` in `{0, 1}` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
| three `_SeqAllToAll.apply` calls, one each for q, k, v | one call on a `3 * head_dim` last axis: one handshake instead of three, same bytes |
| `batch_dim_idx=1`, i.e. `(s, b, n, d)` | not accepted — transpose first, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
| `uneven_heads_all2all`, sizes derived from `get_num_kv_heads()`, `assert async_op == False` | `head_splits=[...]` that you pass, on the sync **and** the async call |
| `UlyssesSPAttentionHF` (ALST), strictly `(sl, bs, hc, hs)` | not accepted — transpose in and back out, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
| the `_SeqAllToAll` `torch.autograd.Function` wrapper | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |
| `UlyssesSPDataLoaderAdapter`, `register_with_transformers()`, `UlyssesSPFwdLossBwdWithLogits` | no counterpart — this is a collective, not a training integration |

`DistributedAttention.forward`'s fourth parameter is `batch_dim_idx`, positional and required. If
your call site passes an attention mask there — the DeepSpeed tutorial snippet and
Megatron-DeepSpeed's non-flash branch both do — the layout selection is reading a tensor, and you
should settle what that call actually did before porting it.

| what you write today | what it becomes here |
| --- | --- |
| `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
| `_usp_output_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
| `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=1)`, i.e. `(b, n, s, d)` | not accepted — transpose first, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
| `_usp_input_all_to_all_qkv` (4D q/k/v) / `_usp_input_all_to_all_packed_qkv` (3D q/k/v) — both pack the three into one collective | one `all_to_all_4d` on `(b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)`, which is the same packing expressed as a shape |
| `_usp_input_all_to_all_varlen(x, seq_lens, head_dim=2)` and its output form | `seq_splits=seq_lens, head_splits=[n_global // ws] * ws` on the ordinary call; there is no separate varlen entry point |
| `sequence_model_parallel_all_to_all_4D(x, scatter_dim=2, gather_dim=1)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
| `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D.apply(...)` | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |
| `_a2a_staging_buffer(role, shape, dtype, device)`, bypassed when `torch.is_grad_enabled()` | nothing to pass or plumb: windows are cached internally per dtype and stream, with grad on or off |
| `_ipc_all_to_all_4d`, gated to `world_size == 2` | the copy-engine path is the only path, at every `world_size` in `[1, 8]` |

support, and `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D`, which is differentiable and reaches the same result
through different permutes. Both map to the same two calls here.

| `SeqAllToAll4D.apply(pg, x, 2, 1)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
| `SeqAllToAll4D.apply(pg, x, 1, 2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |

| `use_sync=True` | no counterpart; nothing here inserts a `torch.cuda.synchronize()` |

| --- | --- |
| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx = 2` | `mode=0` |
| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx` in `{0, 1}` | `mode=1` |
| yunchang `scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=1` | `mode=0` |
| yunchang `scatter_idx=1, gather_idx=2` | `mode=1` |
| sglang `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=0` |
| sglang `_usp_output_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=1` |
| sglang `scatter_dim=2, gather_dim=1` | `mode=0` |

- **An attention kernel.** No `attn_type`, no kernel selection, no q/k/v plumbing — you call your own.
- **`torch.compile` tracing.** A meta kernel propagates shapes under `FakeTensor` and AOTAutograd,
  but a module holding an `UlyssesGroup` graph-breaks: the group is a torchbind object with no
  registered fake class.
- **Autograd on the async form or with `out=`**, and **3D or 5D entry points**.
- **dtypes** beyond `float16` / `bfloat16` / `float32` / `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` / `int8` /
  `uint8`, with `d * elem_size` 16-byte aligned.

## After the switch

- **Construction, `empty_output()` and `destroy()` are collective**, and **every rank must issue the
  same sequence of shapes and dtypes** — a new shape allocates a window collectively. Violating it
  hangs; nothing raises and nothing times out. This is the same discipline the collectives you are
  leaving already require, applied to allocation as well as to the call.
- Build the group **once** and keep it. It holds the windows, the plan cache and the comm stream.
- Pass `out=` from `empty_output()` to remove the copy-out, worth a further 1.14–1.28×. Allocate the
  buffer outside the loop; it is collective. **Not in a training graph**: `out=` reaches a mutating
  op with no autograd formula, so the result comes back detached and nothing raises. See
  [quickstart.md](quickstart.md).

1	# Quick start
2	
3	## Wrapping attention
4	
5	The two calls bracket attention: mode 0 trades the sequence shard for a head shard, mode 1 trades
6	it back.
7	
8	```python
9	import os
10	
11	import torch
12	import torch.distributed as dist
13	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
14	
15	dist.init_process_group("nccl")
16	torch.cuda.set_device(int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"]))
17	ws = dist.get_world_size()
18	
19	group = UlyssesGroup()          # collective; refuses a group that is not NVLink-joined
20	
21	def attention_block(qkv):       # (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
22	    qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)      # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
23	    out = attention(qkv)                        # each rank now holds whole sequences
24	    return group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)     # -> (b, s_local, n_global, head_dim)
25	```
26	
27	Pack q, k and v into one collective when you can: the last dim is just `3 * head_dim`, and one
28	call moves the same bytes with one handshake instead of three.
29	
30	## Removing the copy-out
31	
32	The default returns a tensor the call allocated, which costs one flat device-to-device copy out of
33	the window. Give it a symmetric buffer instead and the peers write that buffer directly:
34	
35	```python
36	buf = group.empty_output(qkv, mode=0)     # collective: allocate ONCE, outside the loop
37	for step in range(steps):
38	    y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, out=buf)   # no copy-out; y is buf
39	```
40	
41	`buf` is an ordinary tensor you own. It is overwritten by the next call that uses it, so use one
42	buffer per concurrent call.
43	
44	`out=` gives up the gradient: the result comes back with no `grad_fn` and no `requires_grad`, and
45	nothing raises. Use it in inference and under `torch.no_grad()`; inside a training graph, call
46	without `out=`.
47	
48	## Overlapping with compute
49	
50	The transfer uses no SMs, so it can run underneath compute. Submit it, do the compute, then use the
51	result — the first aten op on it inserts the wait GPU-side.
52	
53	```python
54	y = group.all_to_all_4d_async(qkv, mode=0)   # inference only: raises if qkv requires grad
55	h = some_gemm_chain(other_input)             # runs while the copy engines move qkv
56	y = y.wait()                                 # or just use y; the first op waits by itself
57	```
58	
59	The async form is not differentiable and refuses a grad-requiring input rather than dropping the
60	gradient, so in a training step this is the sync call's job.
61	
62	Wait on, or use, every async result. A dropped one leaves an entry in torch's work registry.
63	
64	## Dropping the sequence padding
65	
66	Sharding a sequence usually means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size and padding the
67	tail, so every rank holds the same length. Those padded tokens then ride through attention and the
68	collective on every layer of every step. Pass the real per-rank lengths instead:
69	
70	```python
71	s = 75827                                    # does not divide by ws
72	seq_splits = [s // ws + (1 if p < s % ws else 0) for p in range(ws)]
73	head_splits = [n_global // ws] * ws
74	
75	y = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0, seq_splits=seq_splits, head_splits=head_splits)
76	```
77	
78	Both lists or neither, identical on every rank. Uneven is the general path here, not a slow one.
79	
80	## Under 2-D parallelism
81	
82	`process_group` takes any subgroup — the sp slice of a tp × sp mesh, with no restriction on which
83	ranks it contains:
84	
85	```python
86	sp_group = mesh["sp"].get_group()
87	group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)
88	```
89	
90	## What will hang you
91	
92	Every rank must issue the same sequence of shapes. The first call with a new shape allocates a
93	window, and that allocation is collective — if one rank takes a branch the others do not, it waits
94	there. This is the same discipline `torch.distributed` collectives already require.
95	
96	## Coming from another Ulysses
97	
98	`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention` and `LongContextAttention` are attention modules, and
99	sglang's `usp.py` is called from one; this is only the collective, so a port replaces the module
100	with the two calls above plus your own attention. `scatter_idx` / `gather_idx` map to `mode`, the
101	`torch.autograd.Function` wrapper is deleted rather than translated, and a caller on `(s, b, n, d)`
102	still owes a transpose. Call by call: [migration.md](migration.md).
103	
104	## Checking the machine
105	
106	```bash
107	fast-ulysses doctor
108	```
109	
110	Prints the build, the devices, and the pairwise NVLink matrix. A group spanning a pair marked `N`
111	is refused at construction.

3	Coming from DeepSpeed-Ulysses, sglang's `usp.py` or yunchang: what each call becomes here, what your
4	layout costs, and what this library does not have.
5	
6	One structural difference first. All three of those ship an **attention module** —
7	`DistributedAttention`, `UlyssesAttention`, `LongContextAttention` — that owns the q/k/v exchange,
8	the attention call and the output exchange. fast-ulysses ships **only the collective**. You replace
9	one module with two calls and your own attention kernel. `examples/dit_attention.py` is that shape
10	end to end, forward and backward.
11	
12	Left-hand cells below were read from: DeepSpeed `deepspeed/sequence/layer.py` and
13	`deepspeed/runtime/sequence_parallel/ulysses_sp.py`; sglang
14	`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/usp.py` and
15	`runtime/distributed/{communication_op.py,device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py}`;
16	yunchang `yunchang/comm/all_to_all.py`, `yunchang/ulysses/attn_layer.py`, `yunchang/globals.py` and
17	`yunchang/hybrid/attn_layer.py`. Read on the default branch on 2026-08-10, not from a pinned
18	release; yunchang's default branch and its latest tag, 0.6.4, are identical in `comm/all_to_all.py`.
19	Check your installed version before trusting a row.
20	
21	## The shape of the replacement
22	
23	```python
24	# DeepSpeed
25	from deepspeed.sequence.layer import DistributedAttention
26	
27	self.dist_attn = DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)
28	out = self.dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx)   # 0 -> (b, s, n, d), 1 -> (s, b, n, d)
29	```
30	
31	```python
32	# here -- qkv packed into the last axis, so two collectives stay two collectives
33	from fast_ulysses import UlyssesGroup
34	
35	group = UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)   # collective; build once, not per call
36	
37	# qkv is this rank's shard, (b, s_local, n_global, 3 * head_dim)
38	qkv = group.all_to_all_4d(qkv, mode=0)   # -> (b, s_global, n_local, 3 * head_dim)
39	q, k, v = qkv.chunk(3, dim=-1)
40	out = local_attn(q, k, v)                # your kernel, on whole sequences
41	out = group.all_to_all_4d(out, mode=1)   # (b, s_global, n_local, hd) -> (b, s_local, n, hd)
42	```

44	## From DeepSpeed-Ulysses
45	
46	| what you write today | what it becomes here |
47	| --- | --- |
48	| `DistributedAttention(local_attn, sp_group, scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=0)` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_group)` — the collective only; you call `local_attn` yourself |
49	| `dist_attn(q, k, v, batch_dim_idx=0)` | `all_to_all_4d(t, mode=0)` per tensor, or one call on q/k/v packed into a `3 * head_dim` last axis |
50	| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, 2, g, batch_dim_idx)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)` |
51	| `_SeqAllToAll.apply(pg, x, g, 2, batch_dim_idx)` — the output call, indices swapped, `g` in `{0, 1}` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
52	| three `_SeqAllToAll.apply` calls, one each for q, k, v | one call on a `3 * head_dim` last axis: one handshake instead of three, same bytes |
53	| `batch_dim_idx=1`, i.e. `(s, b, n, d)` | not accepted — transpose first, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
54	| `uneven_heads_all2all`, sizes derived from `get_num_kv_heads()`, `assert async_op == False` | `head_splits=[...]` that you pass, on the sync **and** the async call |
55	| `UlyssesSPAttentionHF` (ALST), strictly `(sl, bs, hc, hs)` | not accepted — transpose in and back out, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
56	| the `_SeqAllToAll` `torch.autograd.Function` wrapper | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |
57	| `UlyssesSPDataLoaderAdapter`, `register_with_transformers()`, `UlyssesSPFwdLossBwdWithLogits` | no counterpart — this is a collective, not a training integration |
58	
59	`DistributedAttention.forward`'s fourth parameter is `batch_dim_idx`, positional and required. If
60	your call site passes an attention mask there — the DeepSpeed tutorial snippet and
61	Megatron-DeepSpeed's non-flash branch both do — the layout selection is reading a tensor, and you
62	should settle what that call actually did before porting it.

74	| `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D.apply(...)` | nothing: `all_to_all_4d` is differentiable |

78	sglang has two implementations of this collective — `usp.py`'s plain functions, with no gradient
79	support, and `DistributedAutograd.AllToAll4D`, which is differentiable and reaches the same result
80	through different permutes. Both map to the same two calls here.

82	## From yunchang / long-context-attention
83	
84	| what you write today | what it becomes here |
85	| --- | --- |
86	| `set_seq_parallel_pg(...)` writing the module-level `PROCESS_GROUP.ULYSSES_PG` | `UlyssesGroup(process_group=sp_pg)` per instance; no global state |

89	| `SeqAllToAll4D.apply(pg, x, 1, 2)` | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=1)` |
90	| `all_to_all_4D(x, 2, 1, group=pg)` — the plain function, no grad | `group.all_to_all_4d(x, mode=0)`, which does carry grad |
91	| `all_to_all_5D(x, scatter_idx=3, ...)` on `(bs, s, 3, hc, hs)` | no 5D entry point — fold the qkv axis, see [Layouts](#layouts) |
92	| `use_pack_qkv=True`, `torch.cat([q, k, v])` on the batch axis — the branch then calls `.continous()`, which is not a tensor method, so it raises `AttributeError` before the collective | that cat works unchanged (`b` becomes `3 * b`); packing into `3 * head_dim` is the same one handshake |

95	| a head count that does not divide `world_size` (fails at yunchang's `reshape`) | `head_splits=[...]` |
96	
97	yunchang enforces the index pair — only `(2, 1)` and `(1, 2)` are implemented, anything else raises —
98	so its two directions map one-to-one onto the two modes.
99	
100	## scatter_idx / gather_idx, and mode
101	
102	`mode=0` scatters heads and gathers sequence: `(b, s_local, n_global, d) -> (b, s_global, n_local, d)`.
103	`mode=1` is the inverse.
104	
105	| what selects the direction today | here |
106	| --- | --- |
107	| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx = 2` | `mode=0` |
108	| DeepSpeed `scatter_idx` in `{0, 1}` | `mode=1` |
109	| yunchang `scatter_idx=2, gather_idx=1` | `mode=0` |
110	| yunchang `scatter_idx=1, gather_idx=2` | `mode=1` |
111	| sglang `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=0` |
112	| sglang `_usp_output_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` | `mode=1` |
113	| sglang `scatter_dim=2, gather_dim=1` | `mode=0` |
114	
115	Two traps in the left column:
116	
117	- **DeepSpeed's `gather_idx` does not select the layout on the even path.** It is never passed to
118	  `_generate_layout_params`, and in `single_all_to_all` it is forwarded only to
119	  `uneven_heads_all2all`; the direction is chosen by the predicate `scatter_idx < 2` alone.
120	  `gather_idx` matters only because the output call swaps it into `scatter_idx`. Map by
121	  `scatter_idx`, not by the argument names.
122	- **yunchang's `all_to_all_4D` docstring contradicts its own signature** (it says the defaults are
123	  `scatter_idx=1, gather_idx=2`; the signature is `2, 1`). Read the signature.
124	
125	## Layouts
126	
127	This library takes **4D `(b, s, n, d)` and nothing else.** No 3D form, no 5D form, no
128	`batch_dim_idx`, no `head_dim` argument. That is a real constraint and it is where a migration
129	costs something.
130	
131	| the layout you have | what it costs here |
132	| --- | --- |
133	| `(b, s, n, d)` — sglang `head_dim=2`, yunchang, DeepSpeed `batch_dim_idx=0` | nothing; this is the input |
134	| `(3, s, n, d)` — a q/k/v stack whose dim 0 is not batch | nothing; `b = 3`, and q, k, v are exchanged independently |
135	| `(s, n * d)` contiguous 3D | `x.view(1, s, n, d)` — a view, no copy |
136	| `(b, n, s, d)` — sglang `head_dim=1`, and sglang's default | `x.transpose(1, 2)` in, and back out after the call. Each of those is the size of one of the two permutes this library removes: half the saving goes back if your attention kernel takes the output as a strided view, all of it if it wants contiguous both ways |
137	| `(s, b, n, d)` — Megatron native, DeepSpeed `batch_dim_idx=1`, ALST `UlyssesSPAttentionHF` | `x.transpose(0, 1)` in and back out. Megatron's flash path already pays exactly this (`rearrange("s b ... -> b s ...").contiguous()`) before DeepSpeed's own permutes, so for that caller it is a wash; for ALST, which stays sequence-first end to end, it is a new cost |
138	| `(b, s, 3, n, d)` — yunchang's 5D | fold the qkv axis to `(b, s, n, 3 * d)`, one permute, or emit the projection in that order upstream as `examples/dit_attention.py` does |
139	
140	`.contiguous()` is applied internally, so writing it yourself changes nothing — but a transposed
141	input is copied either way, by you or by the op.
142	
143	The 5D fold has a shortcut that looks right and is not. `(b, s, 3, n, d)` reshapes to
144	`(b, s, 3 * n, d)` for free, but an even split then cuts that merged axis into contiguous chunks, so
145	a rank receives a mixture of q, k and v heads rather than the same head slice of each.
146	
147	## Autograd: there is no wrapper to port
148	
149	DeepSpeed's `_SeqAllToAll` and yunchang's `SeqAllToAll4D` are `torch.autograd.Function`s whose
150	`backward` re-applies the forward with `scatter_idx` and `gather_idx` swapped. `all_to_all_4d` is
151	differentiable in C++, so the wrapper is deleted, not translated: the backward is the other `mode`.
152	
153	The convention differs where it matters. Those libraries express the backward as *swap the two
154	indices*; here it is *the other mode with the **same** splits*. Identical while shards are even,
155	not once they are not — why, in [api.md](api.md).
156	
157	`examples/dit_attention.py` is the worked case — one DiT attention block, sequence-parallel, an
158	ordinary `nn.Module`, checked for both output and input gradient against the same block with no
159	sequence parallelism, then run through five optimiser steps:
160	
161	```bash
162	torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 examples/dit_attention.py
163	```
164	
165	Two exceptions. `all_to_all_4d_async` is not differentiable and raises on a grad-requiring input
166	rather than dropping the gradient silently. `out=` is not differentiable either and raises for the
167	same reason: the value handed back is the caller's own buffer. Both are accepted under
168	`torch.no_grad()`; keep them out of the training graph.
169	
170	## Uneven shards, which is the reason to move
171	
172	| library | uneven support |
173	| --- | --- |
174	| DeepSpeed | heads only, via `uneven_heads_all2all`, with sizes derived from `get_num_kv_heads()` rather than passed by the caller; `assert async_op == False`. No uneven sequence |
175	| sglang `usp.py` | sequence only. `_usp_*_varlen` take `seq_lens`, the group's per-rank sequence shards with `s_local == seq_lens[rank]` asserted, which is what `seq_splits` is. Heads still have to divide: `assert h_global % world_size == 0` |
176	| yunchang | none. `hc // world_size` then a `reshape`, so a non-divisible head count fails at the reshape with no explicit check |
177	| here | `seq_splits` / `head_splits`, both or neither, identical on every rank, on the sync and async calls alike. Even splits are the special case of the same code path, not a fast path beside it |
178	
179	What that buys: sharding a sequence normally means rounding it up to a multiple of the group size,
180	and those padded tokens then ride through attention and both collectives on every layer of every
181	step. Dropping the pad costs the baseline **5–11%** and costs this path **1.00–1.03×** — every
182	shape, every machine. Table in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md), "Removing the sequence padding".
183	
184	## The measured baseline is the path you are leaving
185	
186	The `BASE` column in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md) is not a strawman built for the comparison. It is
187	sglang's `_usp_input_all_to_all(x, head_dim=2)` restated permute for permute —
188	`benchmark/bench_a2a.py:baseline_stages`:
189	
190	```python
191	y = x.permute(2, 0, 1, 3).contiguous().flatten()
192	dist.all_to_all_single(recv, y, group=pg)
193	recv.reshape(ws, h_local, b, s_local, d).permute(2, 0, 3, 1, 4).contiguous().reshape(...)
194	```
195	
196	`test/distributed/correctness.py:reference_even` holds this operator **bit-exact** against that same
197	path, so the two are checked to be the same function before either is timed. The **1.60–2.17×** in
198	that document, and the per-machine multipliers in the README, are therefore measured against exactly
199	what a sglang or DeepSpeed caller runs today, and the `relayout%` column — **46.9–60.0%** of the
200	baseline — is the two permute kernels that do not exist on this side.
201	
202	Two qualifications, so the number is read for what it is:
203	
204	- The benchmark measures `mode=0`. Upstream sglang's `mode=1` equivalent, `_usp_output_all_to_all`
205	  at `head_dim=2`, already replaces its second permute with a fused CUDA kernel — `usp_merge_heads`
206	  from `sglang.kernels.ops.diffusion.usp_relayout`, JIT-built from `diffusion/usp_relayout.cuh`,
207	  with `x.permute(2, 1, 0, 3, 4).contiguous()` as its own fallback. Its cost was not measured here,
208	  so against *current* sglang the saving on the mode-1 half is smaller than the table implies, by an
209	  unknown amount. Mode 0's two permutes are real on both.
210	- The multiplier moves with world size, for the baseline's reason rather than this operator's — at
211	  ws=4 it is 2.6–2.8× on B200 and 1.7–1.9× on H100. Compare `relayout%` across group sizes, not
212	  the multiplier; the table and the reason are in [benchmark.md](benchmark.md).
213	
214	## What this does not have
215	
216	Check this list before you start, not after.
217	
218	- **Cross-node.** One node. Nothing routes over a NIC.
219	- **PCIe.** `UlyssesGroup()` refuses a group whose GPUs are not NVLink-joined; `require_nvlink=False`
220	  exists to measure that case, not to run in it. Across a CPU socket this path measured 0.62× and
221	  0.14× of `torch.distributed` on two PCIe nodes — if your group is not NVLink-joined, stay where
222	  you are.
223	- **`world_size > 8`.** Structural: `BarPeers::p[8]` in `src/barrier.cu`.
224	- **Ring attention and the ulysses × ring hybrid.** `LongContextAttention` has no counterpart.
225	- **An attention kernel.** No `attn_type`, no kernel selection, no q/k/v plumbing — you call your own.
226	- **`torch.compile` tracing.** A meta kernel propagates shapes under `FakeTensor` and AOTAutograd,
227	  but a module holding an `UlyssesGroup` graph-breaks: the group is a torchbind object with no
228	  registered fake class.
229	- **Autograd on the async form or with `out=`**, and **3D or 5D entry points**.
230	- **dtypes** beyond `float16` / `bfloat16` / `float32` / `float8_e4m3fn` / `float8_e5m2` / `int8` /
231	  `uint8`, with `d * elem_size` 16-byte aligned.
232	
233	## After the switch
234	
235	- **Construction, `empty_output()` and `destroy()` are collective**, and **every rank must issue the
236	  same sequence of shapes and dtypes** — a new shape allocates a window collectively. Violating it
237	  hangs; nothing raises and nothing times out. This is the same discipline the collectives you are
238	  leaving already require, applied to allocation as well as to the call.

241	  buffer outside the loop; it is collective. **Not in a training graph**: `out=` reaches a mutating
242	  op with no autograd formula, so the result comes back detached and nothing raises. See

2	/// @file
3	/// The two device-side pieces of one collective: the copy-engine transfer and the flag barrier.
4	/// Neither knows where the peer addresses came from -- the caller passes them in, which is what

13	/// @brief Issue `plan.ops` as pitched cudaMemcpy2D/3DAsync copies into the peers' windows.
14	///
15	/// Remote peers are serialised on `xfer` because they all leave through the same egress and
16	/// separate streams would only make them contend; this rank's own share crosses no link and runs
17	/// on `stream` alongside them. The transfer is joined back onto `stream` before returning.
18	///
19	/// The zero-SM property is a property of the REMOTE copies: a peer copy overlaps concurrent compute,
20	/// while a same-device copy competes with it for the same memory system. This rank's own share is a
21	/// same-device copy, and so is the copy-out on the copying path.
22	///
23	/// @param src        base of this rank's input tensor
24	/// @param peer_ptrs  peer p's window base, as addressed from this rank; `plan.ops` offsets are
25	///                   relative to it. Its size is the world size.
26	/// @param plan       what this rank sends, from build_plan()
27	/// @param xfer       the group's dedicated transfer stream
28	/// @param rank       this rank's index within `peer_ptrs`
29	/// @param stream     the caller's stream
30	void launch_a2a_ce(const void*                  src,
31	                   const std::vector<uint64_t>& peer_ptrs,
32	                   const A2APlan&               plan,
33	                   cudaStream_t                 xfer,
34	                   int                          rank,
35	                   cudaStream_t                 stream);
36	
37	/// @brief Barrier across the group, over P2P-accessible flags.
38	///
39	/// A one-block spin kernel: rank r publishes its epoch into every peer's `flags[r]` with a release
40	/// store, then waits until its own `flags[0..ws-1]` have all reached that epoch. The epoch lives on
41	/// the device and is advanced by the kernel, so a captured graph advances it on replay too -- a
42	/// host-computed epoch would bake a constant into the graph and every replay would be satisfied by
43	/// stale state.
44	///
45	/// The layout inside each rank's flag region is `uint64 flags[ws]` followed by `uint64 epoch`, so
46	/// the caller must provide at least `(ws + 1) * 8` bytes and zero them before the first call.
47	///
48	/// @param stream     the stream to order the handshake on
49	/// @param flag_ptrs  peer p's flag region, as addressed from this rank. Its size is the world size.
50	/// @param rank       this rank's index within `flag_ptrs`
51	void fast_barrier(cudaStream_t stream, const std::vector<uint64_t>& flag_ptrs, int rank);

54	///

58	/// caller's stream, so the test for that assumption has a negative control. 0 disarms.
59	void set_ce_fault(int64_t delay_us);

106	    /// falling back to a copy, since the fallback would be a local decision too.
107	    const Window& lend_window(at::ScalarType dtype, int64_t numel);
108	
109	    /// @brief The window `out` is, or nullptr when it is an ordinary tensor.
110	    const Window* window_of(const at::Tensor& out) const;
111	
112	    // (shape, dtype) -> staging buffer + the event saying the comm stream is done reading it.
113	    struct Staging {
114	        at::Tensor  tensor;
115	        cudaEvent_t release = nullptr;
116	    };
117	
118	    /// @brief Staging buffer for the async path, so the caller's tensor is never retained
119	    /// cross-stream. Copies `x` into it on `caller`, then makes `comm` wait for that copy.
120	    ///
121	    /// Buffers of a shape form a pool rather than a single slot, so several async calls of the
122	    /// SAME shape can be in flight at once -- which is what splitting one packed exchange into
123	    /// per-tensor ones does. With one slot the second call's copy waits, ON THE CALLER'S STREAM,
124	    /// for the first exchange to retire, serialising the very compute it was issued early to
125	    /// overlap. Sharing a slot is still correct, just not concurrent.
126	    ///
127	    /// @return the slot used; pass it to release_staging() once the transfer has been issued.
128	    Staging* stage(const at::Tensor& x, c10::cuda::CUDAStream caller, cudaStream_t comm);
129	
130	    /// @brief Record, on `comm`, that `slot` may be overwritten again.
131	    ///
132	    /// noexcept because it runs from a scope guard that must also fire while an exception from the
133	    /// transfer is propagating. Unchecked for the same reason, and it costs nothing: a checked
134	    /// record that failed would leave exactly the state an unchecked one does.
135	    void release_staging(Staging* slot, cudaStream_t comm) noexcept;
136	
137	    cudaStream_t xfer_stream();
138	
139	    /// @brief TESTS ONLY. This rank's barrier epoch for the window `probe` belongs to -- itself,
140	    /// when it came from make_output(), otherwise `role`'s window for its dtype. -1 when neither
141	    /// exists yet. Synchronising, and it reads a counter the barrier kernel owns: it is here so a
142	    /// CUDA-graph replay can be shown to advance the epoch rather than announce a stale one.
143	    int64_t epoch(const at::Tensor& probe, WindowRole role) const;
144	
145	    /// @brief TESTS ONLY. How many staging slots exist for `like`'s (shape, dtype); 0 before the
146	    /// first async call of that shape. Whether two same-shaped calls got separate buffers is the
147	    /// whole point of the pool and is invisible in the results: sharing one corrupts only when the
148	    /// timing lines up, so a bit-exact pair proves nothing on its own and the count does.
149	    int64_t staging_slots(const at::Tensor& like) const;
150	
151	    /// @brief Release the windows and the transfer stream. Buffers handed out by make_output are
152	    /// the caller's and are unaffected.
153	    void destroy();
154	
155	private:
156	    struct PlanKey {
157	        std::vector<int64_t> sizes;
158	        // optional, not vector: an absent split list and an EMPTY one are different calls -- the
159	        // first is the even special case and the second is an error -- and as bare vectors they
160	        // are the same key, so the empty one would hit the even plan and skip its own rejection.
161	        std::optional<std::vector<int64_t>> seq, head;
162	        int64_t                             mode;
163	        at::ScalarType                      dtype;
164	        bool                                operator<(const PlanKey& o) const;
165	    };
166	
167	    /// Allocate `numel` elements of symmetric memory, rendezvous, and clear the handshake region.
168	    Window allocate(int64_t numel, at::ScalarType dtype);
169	
170	    std::string  group_name_;
171	    int          rank_, world_size_, device_index_;
172	    cudaStream_t xfer_      = nullptr;
173	    bool         destroyed_ = false;
174	
175	    std::map<PlanKey, A2APlan>                           plans_;
176	    std::map<std::pair<int64_t, at::ScalarType>, Window> windows_;
177	    std::map<const void*, Window>                        owned_;  // handed to callers, by address
178	
179	    // Lent output windows, per dtype: a fixed rotation, so the same call picks the same slot on
180	    // every rank. Four is a packed exchange split into q/k/v with one still in flight; a caller
181	    // holding more lent results than this at once is refused rather than slowed down, because
182	    // every way of slowing it down would be a decision this rank makes alone.
183	    static constexpr size_t kLentSlots = 4;
184	
185	    struct LentPool {
186	        std::vector<Window> slots;  // grown to kLentSlots, then rotated through
187	        size_t              calls = 0;
188	    };
189	    std::map<at::ScalarType, LentPool> lent_;
190	
191	    // Concurrent in-flight exchanges of one shape. Four covers a split q/k/v with room to spare;
192	    // past the bound a call waits for a slot rather than growing without limit, since every slot
193	    // pins a full input's worth of device memory -- and stage()'s own bound of 16 shapes is
194	    // therefore 16 * this many buffers.
195	    static constexpr size_t kMaxStagingPerShape = 4;
196	
197	    // (shape, dtype) -> pool of staging buffers. unique_ptr because callers hold a Staging* across
198	    // the transfer, and growing the pool must not move the slots already handed out.
199	    std::map<std::pair<std::vector<int64_t>, at::ScalarType>, std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Staging>>> staging_;
200	};
201	
202	}  // namespace ulysses

14	///
15	/// Remote peers are serialised on `xfer` because they all leave through the same egress and
16	/// separate streams would only make them contend; this rank's own share crosses no link and runs
17	/// on `stream` alongside them. The transfer is joined back onto `stream` before returning.
18	///
19	/// The zero-SM property is a property of the REMOTE copies: a peer copy overlaps concurrent compute,
20	/// while a same-device copy competes with it for the same memory system. This rank's own share is a
21	/// same-device copy, and so is the copy-out on the copying path.
22	///
23	/// @param src        base of this rank's input tensor

25	///                   relative to it. Its size is the world size.

31	                   const std::vector<uint64_t>& peer_ptrs,

33	                   cudaStream_t                 xfer,

38	///
39	/// A one-block spin kernel: rank r publishes its epoch into every peer's `flags[r]` with a release
40	/// store, then waits until its own `flags[0..ws-1]` have all reached that epoch. The epoch lives on
41	/// the device and is advanced by the kernel, so a captured graph advances it on replay too -- a
42	/// host-computed epoch would bake a constant into the graph and every replay would be satisfied by
43	/// stale state.

46	/// the caller must provide at least `(ws + 1) * 8` bytes and zero them before the first call.
47	///

50	/// @param rank       this rank's index within `flag_ptrs`
51	void fast_barrier(cudaStream_t stream, const std::vector<uint64_t>& flag_ptrs, int rank);
52	
53	/// @brief TESTS ONLY: publish the closing flag before the payload has landed, on purpose.
54	///
55	/// The operator assumes a completed copy-engine write is visible at the destination by the time a
